trust_decision.summary: Whether a publish-service reader (RoleReader/RoleVisitor, injected for every proxied request) may read a static resource: the REST API applies publish rules (DisabledInPublish filters, templates denied, per-document publish access), but the kernel's static-file route handlers in kernel/server/serve.go only call CheckAuth, which admits readers.

landing_point.why: The summary names templates first, and serveTemplates sits beside serveSnippets and serveExport in the one file that registers static routes. The neighbouring /assets/ handler already shows the reader publish-access pattern at kernel/server/serve.go:760-766.

fix_sites.entry_point: new model helpers called from the /widgets/, /plugins/, /emojis/, /snippets/ handlers (kernel/model/publish_resource_access.go)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: kernel/server/serve.go:465-479 (snippets filesystem fallback 'look on the filesystem when not found in conf.json'); fixed so readers get 404 there (fix.diff:472-482, test fix.diff:784-786)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Files in data/snippets that are not in conf.json have no DisabledInPublish flag, so a solver can argue the publish toggle doesn't apply and leave the fallback open to readers. Likewise /plugins/ and /emojis/ aren't named in the summary, and the REST API applies no per-document emoji/widget rule a solver could mirror.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Published pages must keep loading publish-enabled snippets, enabled plugins, and the widgets and custom emojis referenced by documents the reader can access. Admins (including the localhost admin shortcut for /export/) must keep templates and export downloads, a symlinked top-level plugin/widget package directory must still serve, and /public/ stays anonymous. A blanket CheckAdminRole on /widgets/ /plugins/ /emojis/ /snippets/ would break published pages.
